instruction: There's a paper on the Desktop called 2206.08853.pdf. Open its arxiv abstract page in Chrome.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey('f11'); time.sleep(0.5); pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5); pyautogui.scroll(-20)

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent spent 50 turns trying to read the PDF, extract author info via terminal, search Google, and curl arxiv. Never created bookmarks or found author webpages. Failed due to overly complex multi-step task and apt-get errors.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can open terminal (Ctrl+Alt+T), type shell commands, use Chrome address bar, search Google, navigate between terminal and Chrome, find files on filesystem
metadata.failure_analysis: Task required reading PDF, identifying 4 authors, searching for each author's webpage, creating a bookmark folder, and adding 4 bookmarks. Model wasted turns on exploration and apt-get failures. Never reached bookmark creation step.
metadata.task_rationale: Decomposed to simple navigation: identify the arxiv ID from the PDF filename and navigate to the abstract page. Within model's demonstrated ability to use Chrome address bar.
metadata.explanation: Task requires navigating to arxiv.org/abs/2206.08853 in Chrome. Evaluator uses existing is_expected_active_tab metric with active_url_from_accessTree getter to check the active tab URL.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter (active_url_from_accessTree) correctly extracts the active Chrome tab URL via accessibility tree, which is exactly the state needed to verify navigation to the arxiv page.
Metric (is_expected_active_tab) correctly receives the rules dict with type='url' and compares using compare_urls, handling both string and dict input formats.
Expected URL 'https://arxiv.org/abs/2206.08853' is the correct arxiv abstract page for paper 2206.08853, matching the instruction requirement.
Full coverage: the instruction has a single requirement (open arxiv abstract page) and the evaluator checks exactly that.
No postconfig needed: the accessibility tree reads live Chrome state without requiring any dialog to be reopened.
